Article 18
(1) Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector for support in the implementation of protection for women and children in regional areas.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1), are carried out through:
a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), are set forth in the form of a cooperation agreement.

Second Part
Prevention of Acts of Violence, Exploitation and Neglect of Women and Children

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the Region of East Barito Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of Regional Government Administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of East Barito.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives Institution positioned as an element of Government Administration.
5. Regional Apparatus of East Barito Regency is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives of East Barito Regency in the Administration of government affairs that are the authority of East Barito Regency.
6. Dinas is a PD that handles government affairs in the field of women and children.
7. Technical Service Unit is a Regional Technical Service Unit that handles the affairs of protection of Women and children.
8. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
9. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a Woman.
10. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
11. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
12. Violence is any act that results in or causes suffering and distress whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
13. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death.
14. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
15. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual relations, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
16. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
17. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
18. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
19. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
20. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution that has the expertise to provide assistance.
21. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
22. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide Protection.
24. Institution is an agency/dinas/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (LSM) that provides Assistance.
25. Regional Action Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RAD is a foundation and guideline for related dinas, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.
26. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
27. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
28. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral lines up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is the dependent of a woman and/or child.
29. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
30. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the annual financial plan of Regional Government that is discussed and approved jointly by the Regional Government and DPRD and established by Regional Regulation.
31. Gender Equality is the view that all people should receive equal treatment and not be discriminated against based on their gender identity.
32. Medicolegal Service is a form of health service performed by medical personnel using medical science and technology based on the authority possessed for legal purposes and to implement applicable regulations.

CHAPTER III
SCOPE
Article 3 Protection of women and children in the region includes prevention, services, and empowerment for victims of physical violence, psychological violence, sexual violence, exploitation, human trafficking, and domestic neglect including child deviant behavior.
The implementation of protection for women (2) and children from acts of violence is a joint obligation and responsibility among the Regional Government, community, family, and parents.

Article B
The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 5 letters c and d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children

CHAPTER VII
PREVENTION, SERVICES AND EMPOWERMENT
First Part
General Article 10 The Regional Government through the Agency or technical service unit and PD, implements prevention and service efforts for victims of violence, exploitation and neglect of Children and Women up to the empowerment of victims to be able to return to living their lives in accordance with the dignity and honor they possess.

4.4.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, prevention explicitly includes education/awareness-raising activities. Pasal 11(1) lists forms of prevention such as: (a) "kegiatan sosialisasi peraturan perundang undangan terkait dengan perlindungan Anak dan Perempuan kepada masyarakat luas" and (g) "penyuluhan/sosialisasi dalam bentuk penyadaran masyarakat luas hingga ... (keluarga) khususnya para orang tua". These are clearly prevention through education/socialization. The retrieved English candidates (notably [4.4-19] and [4.4-20]) accurately reflect this content, and the judge’s rationale matches the Indonesian provisions. Therefore the pipeline’s 'Yes' is supported by the source text, suggesting the golden label 'No' is likely incorrect.
